name: LTM8049IY#PBF
title: LTM8049: two-channel µModule DC/DC converter, each channel SEPIC or inverting, 2.6 V to 20 V in, ±2.5 V to ±24 V out
summary: A 15 × 9 × 2.42 mm BGA module holding two separate switching converters, each with its switch, coupled inductor, rectifier and some capacitance inside. Each channel runs from 2.6 V to 20 V and becomes a SEPIC (2.5 V to 24 V out) or an inverter (-2.5 V to -24 V out) depending on which output terminal is grounded; one resistor sets each output, one sets each frequency (200 kHz to 2.5 MHz, or synchronised). Each channel has RUN with an accurate threshold for undervoltage lockout, soft-start, power good and a clock output, and the two outputs can be paralleled. A channel delivers at least 1 A at 5 V or -5 V from 12 V.
key_figures: 1A min per channel at VIN = 12V, VOUT = ±5V; 0.25A min at ±24V
0µA typ, 2µA max with RUN = 0V; 10mA typ with RUN = 2V, no load

notes: E and I are temperature grades: the E grade is guaranteed over 0°C to 125°C internal temperature, the I grade over -40°C to 125°C (Note 2). The grade is marked on a label on the shipping container.
Finish codes follow IPC/JEDEC J-STD-609. The module is moisture sensitive and should not go through a second-side reflow.

circuits.title: ±12 V outputs from a 2.7 V to 20 V input
circuits.description: Channel 1 runs as a SEPIC with VOUT1N grounded and gives +12 V; channel 2 runs as an inverter with VOUT2P grounded and gives -12 V. Both RUN pins sit on VIN, so both channels start whenever the input is present. Two 80.6 kΩ resistors set each channel to 1 MHz, and CLKOUT1 drives SYNC2 so channel 2 runs from channel 1's clock while SYNC1 is grounded. The 130 kΩ and 143 kΩ resistors set the two output voltages; 22 µF and 47 µF hold the outputs and two 4.7 µF capacitors bypass the input.
notes: SS1, SS2, PG1, PG2, CLKOUT2, SHARE1 and SHARE2 are not used.

circuits.title: ±5 V converter
circuits.description: The same arrangement as the ±12 V circuit with the recommended ±5 V values: channel 1 is a SEPIC giving +5 V through 45.3 kΩ, channel 2 an inverter giving -5 V through 60.4 kΩ. Both channels run at 750 kHz from 107 kΩ RT resistors, channel 2 clocked from CLKOUT1. The outputs are held by 47 µF and 147 µF.
notes: SS1, SS2, PG1, PG2, CLKOUT2, SHARE1 and SHARE2 are not used.

circuits.title: Paralleled 8 V outputs for more current
circuits.description: Both channels are SEPICs (VOUT1N and VOUT2N grounded) whose positive outputs are joined into one 8 V rail. Each FBX pin has its own 82.5 kΩ resistor to the shared output, and SHARE1 is tied to SHARE2 so the channels split the load. Both run at 1 MHz from 80.6 kΩ, channel 2 clocked from CLKOUT1. One 47 µF capacitor holds the joined output.
notes: SS1, SS2, PG1, PG2 and CLKOUT2 are not used.

circuits.title: Paralleled -5 V outputs for more current
circuits.description: Both channels are inverters (VOUT1P and VOUT2P grounded) whose negative outputs are joined into one -5 V rail. Each FBX pin has its own 60.4 kΩ resistor to the shared output, and SHARE1 is tied to SHARE2. Both run at 750 kHz from 107 kΩ, channel 2 clocked from CLKOUT1. Two 100 µF capacitors from ground to the output hold it.
notes: SS1, SS2, PG1, PG2 and CLKOUT2 are not used.

operation.text: Two independent fixed-frequency current-mode PWM converters share one package. Each holds its controller, power switch, coupled inductor, Schottky rectifier and some input and output capacitance; in channel 1 the two inductor windings are 4.7 µH each, the series coupling capacitor 2.2 µF, the capacitor across the output 0.1 µF and the capacitor on SS 1 nF. Channel 2 is the same except for the CLKOUT2 behaviour with temperature.

Each channel becomes a SEPIC (2.5 V to 24 V) when its VOUTN is grounded, or an inverter (-2.5 V to -24 V) when its VOUTP is grounded. Input range is up to 20 V. At room temperature a channel can deliver 1.5 A with VIN = 12 V and VOUT = 5 V or -5 V. Maximum output current depends on internal temperature and on the size and sign of the output relative to the input.

Pick the row of the recommended-values table for the input range and output voltage and fit its CIN, COUT, RFB and RT. Each channel is set up on its own. The maximum-current curves hold for the recommended operating points; a different frequency can give a different maximum current.

The range is 200 kHz to 2.5 MHz, set by the RT resistor while SYNC is below 0.4 V; RT must never be left open. Too high a frequency lowers efficiency, narrows the usable input range, adds heat and can damage the module under some faults; too low a frequency raises ripple or needs a larger output capacitor.

A clock between 200 kHz and 2.5 MHz on SYNC sets the switching frequency. CLKOUT1 runs about 180° from channel 1 at about 50 % duty and can clock channel 2 or other parts; CLKOUT2 is in phase with channel 2 and its duty cycle follows internal temperature.

When a channel is enabled its SS capacitor is first discharged, which also resets the channel's logic, and then an internal resistor pulls SS up to about 1.8 V, ramping the switch current up gradually. A built-in ramp exists; a capacitor of typically 0.1 µF to 1 µF on SS makes it slower.

RUN has typical thresholds of 1.31 V rising and 1.27 V falling, and sinks 12.1 µA at the rising threshold and about 11.6 µA at the falling one, so one resistor from VIN sets a lockout; a second resistor from RUN to GND reduces the spread caused by the RUN current. A lockout keeps the converter off at low source voltages where a current-limited or high-impedance source could collapse under the converter's constant-power draw.
If VIN falls below about 2.3 V the power switch turns off and the soft-start capacitor is discharged while enough VIN remains; once VIN recovers the channel restarts with a fresh soft-start.

When a channel's output is about 15 % below its target, its switching frequency is reduced, limiting current during faults, overloads and start-up. Above that range it runs at the RT-set frequency. Start-up current depends on load, output capacitance, output voltage, input voltage and frequency, so start-up into the real load needs checking.

An overheated module stops switching and discharges its soft-start capacitor, restarting by itself when it has cooled. The trip point lies above the 125 °C maximum internal rating, so repeated or long activation can reduce reliability.
PGn is an open-drain output that goes high when the channel's feedback is within 4 % of regulation. Its state means something only with RUN above 1.4 V and VIN above 2.6 V.
The two outputs can be joined for more current; SHARE1 and SHARE2 are then tied together, and otherwise left open.

The recommended capacitances are minimums; smaller values are not recommended and larger ones can improve transient response. X5R and X7R ceramics hold their value over temperature and voltage; Y5V and Z5U can lose most of theirs and leave much more ripple. A bulk input capacitor is required.

A ceramic input capacitor and the inductance of the supply wiring form a lightly damped resonance; plugged into a live supply, VIN can ring to more than twice its nominal value and exceed the rating. A small series resistor in VIN, or more commonly an electrolytic bulk capacitor whose ESR damps the ring, prevents this; the bulk capacitor also filters low-frequency ripple and can raise efficiency a little.

Keep RFB and RT next to their pins, and CIN and COUT next to their VIN, VOUT and GND connections, with their ground currents returning right beside or under the module. Tie every GND ball to as large a top-layer copper area as possible, keep the ground between the outside parts and the module unbroken, and join that copper to inner ground planes with many vias, which also carry heat away; smaller via holes call for more vias.

Output current may have to be derated at high ambient temperature or high continuous power, depending on input voltage, output power and ambient. The derating curves were taken with the module on a 58 cm² four-layer FR4 board; other boards behave differently. Most heat leaves through the bottom of the package and the BGA balls into the board, and the die must stay below 125 °C.
